t:
(a) In General.—The Secretary of the Interior shall install in the area of the Lincoln Memorial in the District of Columbia a suitable plaque to commemorate the speech of Martin Luther King, Jr., known as the “I Have A Dream” speech. 
    (b) Relation to Commemorative Works Act.—The Commemorative Works Act (40 U.S.C. 1001 et seq.) shall apply to the design and placement of the plaque within the area of the Lincoln Memorial.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that applying the Commemorative Works Act brings in that Act's review and consultation procedures. But the section itself names no comment period, hearing, advisory body with non-federal members, consultation with outside parties, or right to sue. It only directs the Secretary of the Interior to install a plaque and cross-references another statute, whose review bodies are in any case largely federal. Every actor named in the text is inside the federal government.
fable.s: The Commemorative Works Act (40 U.S.C. 1001 et seq.) shall apply to the design and placement of the plaque within the area of the Lincoln Memorial.

opus.w: The section directs the Secretary of the Interior to install a plaque and applies the Commemorative Works Act to its design and placement. That Act's review process, as I understand it, runs through federal commissions, which are inside the government. The section itself names no states, experts, public comment, hearing, or right to sue, so no outside party takes part in the decision. Reading participation into the cross-reference would mean assuming a process the text never describes.
opus.s: The Commemorative Works Act (40 U.S.C. 1001 et seq.) shall apply to the design and placement of the plaque within the area of the Lincoln Memorial.
opus.b:
**Tempting reading:** Subsection (b) applies the Commemorative Works Act to the plaque's design and placement, and that Act involves review by commissions, so it can look like a participation process.

**Why it fails:** The section names no outside party. The review bodies under the Commemorative Works Act, as I understand them (the Commission of Fine Arts, the National Capital Planning Commission and the National Capital Memorial Advisory Commission), are federal entities. Subsection (a) only tells the Secretary of the Interior to install a plaque. Nothing in the text sets up a comment period, a public hearing, outside membership, consultation with states or tribes, or a right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section mandates the Secretary of the Interior to install a plaque. It does not require consultation with the public, states, or other outside entities before making this decision. The reference to the Commemorative Works Act is a procedural cross-reference, but the section itself does not describe any participation mechanism involving non-federal parties. The action is unilateral by a federal official.
qwen_chat.s: The Secretary of the Interior shall install in the area of the Lincoln Memorial in the District of Columbia a suitable plaque to commemorate the speech of Martin Luther King, Jr., known as the “I Have A Dream” speech.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the "Commemorative Works Act" referenced in subsection (b) contains public participation requirements (such as public hearings or advisory committees), and thus this section implicitly requires participation. However, the section itself does not describe any such process; it merely mandates the installation of a plaque and references another statute for procedural compliance. The definition requires that the *section* involves participation. Mere reference to another law does not constitute participation within this specific text, especially since the primary action (installing a plaque) is a unilateral executive action. Furthermore, even if the Commemorative Works Act requires public input, this section is a specific authorization for a single project, and without explicit text here describing the consultation or public process, we cannot label it as "Yes" based solely on the cross-reference. More importantly, the core action is the Secretary installing a plaque, which is an internal government action.
